_comment: Every product that has appeared in any Breakpoint MCP competitive-analysis sweep,
carried forward permanently.  An entry is never dropped: products that stop moving
are marked `dormant` or `archive` and keep their ruling, so a later sweep does not
re-litigate a question already answered.
`assetlib_version` / `assetlib_modify_date` are what the live Asset Library API
served when this entry was last reconciled; scripts/assetlib_sweep.py compares
the live API against them and reports anything that moved.
`last_analysed` is the date of the last SOURCE-LEVEL pass, which is a stronger
claim than a version check.  When a sweep reports an entry moved, it owes a
source-level pass; when it reports no change, `no change since <last_analysed>`
is a complete and sufficient result for that entry.
House terminology: these are ALTERNATIVE MCP SERVERS, not rivals.  See
docs/LANDSCAPE_TRACKING_POLICY.md.
🆕 291 — THIS ROSTER HAS TWO POPULATIONS, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT.
`entries` are products READ AT SOURCE, each with a ruling: debugger, real_dap_client,
real_lsp_client, csharp, protocol_revision and a note. The cost of a row here is a
source-level pass, so a row is ELECTED and never automatic.
`surfaced` are products a DISCOVERY LEG has seen, carried permanently, holding only
what the leg itself supplies: channel, repository slug, package, version, publish date
and the session that first saw them. No capability claim, because no one has read them.
The cost of a row here is one row, so EVERY project any leg surfaces owes one, and
`assetlib_sweep.py --check` refuses when one is missing.
🔴 WHY IT IS TWO AND NOT ONE. Until 291 the sweep had a single severity — a
never-tracked MCP-shaped entry owed a source-level pass — which was affordable while
the population was ONE channel serving roughly ten new entries a year. The first run
across three channels surfaced fifty. A rule demanding fifty source-level passes in one
commit does not produce fifty analyses; it produces a gate that is red forever and a
roster nobody can make green. Fifty rows with the capability fields blank would be
worse still: that is a coverage claim nobody made.
`channel` records where a product SHIPS, and it is optional. Forty-five entries predate
the channel legs and nobody has recorded where any of them ships; `assetlib_sweep.py
--census` prints that count as `unclassified` rather than defaulting it, so the number
is a visible intake that falls as sessions classify rows.
🆕 323 — `capability_paths` IS AN ALLOW-LIST, AND AN ALLOW-LIST CANNOT HOLD AN ABSENCE.
`capability_paths` names the paths a ruling RESTS ON, so a move touching none of them is
`moved-immaterial`.  That is right for a claim resting on a file and wrong for a claim
resting on the WHOLE TREE — and three of the four capability fields are usually spent as
`false`, which is the claim *we looked and it is not there*.  A commit creating a new
top-level source directory touches no declared path, is priced immaterial, is never
re-read, and the roster keeps publishing an absence the project no longer has.  Twelve
source-level readings at 323 were each asked whether a new top-level directory would
escape their declared paths; twelve of twelve answered yes.
`capability_paths_excluded` is the other half: the entries a session LOOKED AT and ruled
incapable of carrying a capability — documentation, website, samples, media, CI cosmetics.
A path under neither list was classified by nobody, and `material_change` prices that as
UNKNOWN, which is not immaterial.  Immateriality stops being *absent from the watch list*
and becomes *on the list of things somebody ruled harmless*.
🔴 THE FIELD ONLY EVER BUYS STRICTNESS.  An entry declaring paths and no exclusions is
priced exactly as it was before 323, so no row got looser and no red appeared that nobody
asked for.  The five rows that declared paths before 323 owe an exclusion set whenever
they are next read at source.

When it lands, `forge_id` 1309425913 is what survives it and the slug is what will not: `identity_problems` keys `found` by SLUG, so the new name arrives as a stranger and the old one as a row nobody can reach. entries.note: 🔴 323: `real_dap_client` FLIPS FALSE -> TRUE. THIS IS THE ONE COMPETITIVE EVENT IN THIS SWEEP AND IT LANDS ON THE PLANE THIS PROJECT IS DIFFERENTIATED ON. Between the roster's last pass at `e9f41f2` (2026-08-30) and head `a203407`, they shipped src/tools/dap.ts - 1084 lines, a hand-written TypeScript DAP client over node:net to 127.0.0.1:6006 with its own Content-Length framing, request_seq correlation, partial-frame resync and a 1MiB frame cap. PROVEN NEW, not merely unnoticed: an adversarial pass deepened the clone to 873 commits, confirmed e9f41f2 is a true ancestor of HEAD, and `git cat-file -e e9f41f2:src/tools/dap.ts` answers that the file did not exist there. Introduced by 4d684b4 on 2026-09-12 (CHANGELOG 0.32.20), refined by 65ff6ab. 🔴 THE ADVERSARIAL PASS NARROWED THE CLAIM IN THREE WAYS AND EVERY ONE OF THEM MATTERS FOR HOW THIS IS SAID IN PUBLIC. (1) THERE IS NO VARIABLE INSPECTION - `variables`, `scopes` and `evaluate` appear nowhere in the repository; the 18 actions stop at stack_trace, so you can reach a breakpoint and read the call stack and cannot read a value. (2) IT IS NOT IN A DEFAULT INSTALL - src/index.ts:90 defaults the profile to `basic`, which (tool-registry.ts:209) does not contain the `debug` group that owns `dap`, so tools/list on a default install never advertises it; reaching it takes --profile=full or GODOT_MCP_PROFILE=full, an editor connection, and the user manually enabling Editor Settings -> Network -> Debug Adapter. The dispatcher enforces activeGroups rather than the profile, so it is HIDDEN rather than hard-blocked. (3) IT HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST A REAL EDITOR - test/dap.test.ts is 477 lines and 20 real tests, but every one drives a mock TCP server the authors wrote to their own framing assumptions, and CHANGELOG.md:79 concedes 'e2e not covered against a real editor'. Their own v0.33.0 audit records four IMPORTANT defects found in dap after ship, including the `output` action being mathematically dead after 200 messages. 🔵 IT IS A PORT, NOT A WRAPPER AND NOT A CALL-OUT: dap.ts:10 says it was ported from LuoxuanLove-godot-dotnet-mcp's 791-line GDScript executor.gd; no third-party code is vendored, invoked or shelled to, and there is no debug-protocol dependency in the manifest. 🔴 `debugger` IS LEFT AT godot-internal-editor-debugger AND THAT IS NOW A JUDGEMENT, NOT A READING: this head has TWO independent debug paths side by side, and a single-value field cannot say so. The editor-debugger bridge is intact, unchanged and is what a default install gets; the DAP path is the gated one. The DAP fact is carried by real_dap_client, so nothing is lost - but if the roster's convention is `most capable path wins`, this field should read real-dap-client and the editor-debugger fact should move here. FLAGGED FOR RULING, NOT DECIDED. 🔵 csharp HOLDS at true and is NOT the .cs-into-GDScript trap: src/tools/script.ts:576 sets isCsharp and deliberately skips the Godot parse validator, routing .cs to runDotnetBuild (src/tools/shared/validation.ts:64) - gated behind GODOT_MCP_PRIVILEGED_GROUPS=code-execution because MSBuild targets are arbitrary code execution, and degrading to `skipped` when dotnet is off PATH. There is no C# DEBUG path: dap.ts:857 concedes C# breakpoints require a .NET debugger such as coreclr. 🔵 Their own docs name US as the LSP-client holder in a survey of alternative servers (docs/plans/2026-08-05-mcp-ecosystem-research-and-upgrade-plan.md:153).  Ruling holds on the debugger and CHANGES on csharp, which was recorded false and was already true at the previous pass. 9609b06..e9f41f2 is four commits touching three files (+70/-21) and src/ is untouched: instance_registry.gd swapped an instance call to the static FileAccess.set_unix_permissions, which had been aborting _write_instance_json() off Windows, and an e2e test replaced a blind wait with polling. entries.note: 🟢 323: THREE WITHDRAWN FIELDS READ BACK AND `debugger` CLAIMED FOR THE FIRST TIME, at `4d5f491` - the same head the 2026-08-05 pass recorded. 🔴 SCOPE CAVEAT, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: THIS REPOSITORY PUBLISHES ONLY THE FREE GODOT ADDON. README.md:17 states the Node.js MCP server is paid and distributed separately; there is no server/, no package.json and no dependency manifest here. So the DAP and LSP falses are PROVEN FOR THE PUBLISHED HALF and cannot be proven for the closed server. They are still the right call rather than `unknown`: the declared architecture routes all Godot interaction through this plugin, the plugin is the WebSocket CLIENT dialing 6505-6514 with 6005/6006 absent, llms.txt:14-39 enumerates the paid server's full 23-category/162-tool surface with no debugger, C#, LSP or DAP category, and of 163 tool names in settings.local.json exactly one is debug-adjacent. 🔴 THE `debugger` VALUE SITS AT THE DEGENERATE END OF ITS CATEGORY: three UI gestures - find the panel, infer `paused` from whether Continue is enabled, press it. It cannot arm a breakpoint, step, or read a frame. Ruled `godot-internal-editor-debugger` because the vocabulary names control-tree walking and toolbar pressing and both are literally present; it is genuinely borderline with `screen-scrapes-stack-trace-panel`, since no structured debugger data is ever read. 🔴 TWO CLAIMS THE SOURCE DOES NOT SUPPORT: README.md:198 advertises get_editor_errors as returning 'errors and stack traces' while editor_commands.gd:131-141 appends child TreeItem rows verbatim; and .cs is accepted by create_script/edit_script/validate_script while every downstream path is GDScript-only, so validate on a .cs returns 'Could not load script as GDScript' and a contentless create writes `extends Node` into the .cs. That is worse than absent support - it accepts the input and produces broken output. 🔵 CRAFT NOTE (Rule 4): the Continue button is found by comparing Button.icon to the resolved EditorIcons texture rather than by tooltip, explicitly so non-English editors work (issue #34, Italian). 🔴 MONITOR NOTE: if the paid server/ is ever open-sourced it arrives as a brand-new top-level tree carrying whatever DAP/LSP/C# code exists, entirely outside `addons/`.
